answer: Bandwidth proofs tie every seat to a real network pipe. Each epoch a verifier vault streams 256 MB of random chunks tagged with one identity's key, and that identity must forward them to a knoll of 3 randomly drawn peers. Delivery must clear the ledge, a floor of 20 Mbit/s held for the whole transfer, checked by sampled chunk hashes at the peers. Chunks are key-tagged, so one stream can't serve two seats: each fake moves 768 MB per epoch even if never caught, and 500 fakes need 384 GB per epoch over links sustaining 10 Gbit/s.
